{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sc-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"096dcc7e7c2de6afbfc31a7dcd240e9cdad78f4675d5512b732fa9e209a20259","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sc-class-d:lineage:19","source_registry_sha256":"61c32f86a25e3c021742b3c9ddf64a97709817dd75a19df6d2b69eac0a40c4f1","source_liveness_sha256":"feb7871590284d2a19ab0509ff65b48154ba15e637a6ec9b839f55a72736ffdb"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Before you drive: vehicle inspection, seating and mirrors, safety belts, air bags, child passengers, loads and driver assistance features","heading":"C — Tire checks, seat and mirror adjustment, safety belts and air bags, child passenger stages, securing a load and driver assistance (ADAS) features","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Tire checks, seat and mirror adjustment, safety belts and air bags, child passenger stages, securing a load and driver assistance (ADAS) features
Knowledge domain: what a South Carolina driver checks and sets up before moving, from tire pressure and tread to seat, head restraint and mirror positions, correct belt use, air bags, the child restraint stages required by law, load securing and the proper use of driver assistance features.

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
Other drivers and road conditions are outside your control, but keeping your own vehicle and its tires properly maintained is not. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
Crashes caused by neglected tires are preventable, and running on tires that are under-inflated, over-inflated or low on tread creates safety problems. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Check your tire pressure every month using a tire pressure gauge, buying one if you do not already own one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
The correct tire pressure is the PSI number printed on a sticker on the inside doorframe of your vehicle, so note it before measuring. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A02
PSI stands for pounds per square inch, which is how tire pressure is measured. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A02
To take a reading, remove the cap from the valve stem and press the gauge evenly onto it, and measure while the tires are still cold. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A02
For the penny tread test, hold a penny by Lincoln's body and push it, Lincoln's head first, into the groove that looks deepest. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A03
If all of Lincoln's head is visible in the groove, the tread is too worn, so do not drive on those tires and have them replaced. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A03
Sit upright with your back against the seat and your feet on the floor, because slouching can make the vehicle's restraint system less effective. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A03
Set your seat and mirrors before you start driving so you can see clearly, fully control the pedals and steering wheel, and leave room for an air bag to deploy. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A03
In a correct seat position your foot pivots smoothly from the brake to the accelerator while your heel stays on the floor. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A03
The top of the steering wheel should be no higher than the tops of your shoulders. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A03
Leave a gap of at least 10 inches from your chest to the steering wheel, never move the seat so far forward that steering becomes hard, and do not recline the seat. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A03
Head restraints are meant to prevent whiplash, so adjust yours to touch the back of your head rather than sit below ear level. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A03
The rearview mirror, the interior mirror mounted on the windshield, is your primary mirror for seeing what is behind you. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A04
Outside mirrors are set to shrink blind spots, the areas where your view is blocked, and to give the widest possible view to the sides and rear. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A05
For the enhanced left mirror setting, rest your head against the closed window on your left and adjust the mirror until the rear edge of your vehicle barely shows. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A05
Enhanced outside mirror settings hide your own vehicle's sides when you glance at them, but add 12 to 16 degrees of extra viewing area on each side. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A05
Always buckle your own safety belt and make sure every passenger is using a safety belt or a child restraint. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A05
Studies show safety belts greatly cut your chance of injury or death in a collision, keep you from being thrown from the vehicle and help the driver stay in control. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A06
South Carolina has a primary safety belt enforcement law, so an officer with a clear and unobstructed view of a driver or occupant who is unbelted, or not in a child restraint, may stop the driver. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A06
Wear the shoulder harness across your shoulder and chest with little or no slack, never under your arm or behind your back, since that can cause serious internal injuries in a collision. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A06
After fastening, adjust the lap belt so it is snug and sits low across your hips, or you could slide out of it in a collision and be hurt or killed. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A06
Keep wearing safety belts even when your vehicle is equipped with air bags. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A06
Air bags are supplemental restraints designed to work best together with safety belts, lowering the chance that your head and upper body hit the vehicle's interior. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A07
Safety belts put your body in the right position to get the most from the air bag, and your vehicle owner's manual describes the air bags in your vehicle. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A07
A child safety seat must be installed properly and used correctly, and a rear-facing child seat must never be placed in front of an air bag. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A07
Children age seven and younger must ride in a car seat in the back seat so an air bag cannot injure them in a collision. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A07
An infant under age two must be secured in a rear-facing car seat in a rear seat until the child exceeds the seat maker's height or weight limit. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A07
A child at least age two, or a younger child who has outgrown the rear-facing seat's limits, must ride in a forward-facing car seat in a rear seat until exceeding that seat's height or weight limits. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F31 | anchor: A07
A child at least age four who has outgrown the forward-facing car seat must use a booster seat in a rear seat until the adult safety belt fits correctly. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F32 | anchor: A07
A child at least age 8, or at least 57 inches tall, may use an adult safety belt if that belt can secure the child properly. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F33 | anchor: A07
The South Carolina child passenger safety law is SC Code §56-5-6410, and it can be read on the Buckle Up, South Carolina website. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F34 | anchor: A08
Driving with an unsecured load is illegal and very dangerous, and a driver who fails to secure one is guilty of a misdemeanor and may pay a fine plus the cost of cleaning up the spilled material. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F35 | anchor: A08
A load is secure only when nothing can slide, shift, fall or sift onto the road or be blown into the air. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F36 | anchor: A08
Tie a load directly to the vehicle or trailer with rope, netting or straps, and think about covering all of it with a sturdy tarp or netting. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F37 | anchor: A09
Driver assistance safety features in many newer vehicles sense conditions and spot dangers, then either alert you with sounds or vibration or take control by adjusting braking or steering. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-F38 | anchor: A09
Features of this kind include blind spot warning, forward collision warning, automatic emergency braking, a backup camera, active parking assist and lane keeping assistance. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-F39 | anchor: A09
During your driving test you will not be allowed to use certain features, such as parking assist and cruise control. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-F40 | anchor: A09
Assistance features help with the driving task but do not drive the vehicle for you, so you must stay engaged and focused the whole time. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-F41 | anchor: A10
You stay responsible for seeing everything around you through head checks, mirrors and cameras, and for operating the vehicle safely, so never depend on safety features alone. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec05-F42 | anchor: A10
Learn from the owner's manual how your safety features work and where they fall short, because they may not work properly in rain, snow, ice, fog, on hills or in curves. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0052]

Misconceptions: seeing all of Lincoln's head in the penny test means the tread is worn out, not that it is fine; air bags add to safety belts and never replace them; a gauge reading above the doorframe number means letting air out; enhanced mirror settings are meant to hide your own vehicle's sides; assistance features do not drive the car, and some are not allowed on the driving test.
Mnemonics: the child restraint ladder runs rear-facing, forward-facing, booster, then belt, at under two, two and up, four and up, and eight years or fifty-seven inches; for tires, think cold tires, door sticker, match the numbers.
Glossary: PSI means pounds per square inch, the unit of tire pressure; blind spot means an area around the vehicle your mirrors and windows do not show; head restraint means the seat part that limits whiplash; supplemental restraint means a device, such as an air bag, that works alongside the safety belt; primary enforcement means an officer may stop a driver for a belt violation alone; ADAS means advanced driver assistance systems; unsecured load means cargo that can slide, shift, fall, sift or blow off a vehicle.
Dynamic facts: child passenger seat rules, the cited code section and the list of driver assistance features can change; confirm them on the Buckle Up, South Carolina website and the SCDMV website.
